memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "So when the Midianite merchants came by, his brothers pulled Joseph up out of the cistern and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt." - Gen 37:28 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The deed is done. The brothers pull Joseph up out of the pit — not to rescue him, but to sell him. For twenty shekels of silver, the price of a slave, they hand their own brother over to foreign traders bound for Egypt. A beloved son is exchanged for a bag of silver.

It is hard to miss where this quietly points. Centuries later, another beloved brother would be sold for silver — Jesus, betrayed by Judas for thirty pieces of silver (Matt 26:14-15). Strikingly, it was Judah who arranged Joseph's sale, and Judas (the same name) who arranged Jesus'. Joseph — the beloved son, rejected by his brothers, sold for silver, carried off to a far country — is one of Scripture's clearest pictures of Christ.

But watch what God does with this betrayal. The very act meant to destroy Joseph became the road by which he would rise to save many, including the brothers who sold him. In the same way, the betrayal and death of Jesus, the worst crime in history, became the means of the world's salvation (Acts 2:23).

Here is the heart of the gospel hidden in an old story: God takes what human sin means for evil and turns it to good (Gen 50:20). No betrayal, no injustice, no bag of silver can defeat His saving purposes. What looks like the end is often the very place God begins His rescue.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. How does Joseph, sold for silver, point me to Christ?
2. Do I believe God can turn even betrayal into good?
3. Where do I need to trust God's purposes in a painful situation?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that even betrayal for silver could not defeat Your purposes — not for Joseph, and not for Christ. Help me to trust the God who turns evil into good and endings into beginnings. Amen.
